title.en: Who looks after the roads and who the army?

text.en: Your village road is looked after by a local body, the state handles police, and the Union runs the army. Why is power split? That is federalism.

Federalism is a system of government in which power is divided between a central authority and the various units of the country, each with its own powers.
A federation has two levels of government that govern the same citizens and have separate jurisdiction, and the Constitution cannot be changed by one level alone.
The Constitution lists subjects in three lists. The Union List includes defence and foreign affairs, the State List includes police and agriculture, and the Concurrent List includes education and marriage. Residuary subjects go to the Union.
India is described as a 'union of states', and the Parliament can form new states and alter boundaries.
India does not have a national language. Hindi is the official language, and the Constitution recognises 22 scheduled languages.
Linguistic states were created from the 1950s so that each state would have its own language and culture.
A major step towards decentralisation was taken in 1992, when the Constitution was amended to make the third tier of government, local self-government, more powerful.
Panchayati Raj has the gram sabha, gram panchayat, block and zilla parishad levels. At least one-third of positions are reserved for women.
